newsitem.title: USA: Home Depot says profits up 33 pct to new high; stock jumps.
newsitem.headline: Home Depot says profits up 33 pct to new high; stock jumps.

text.p: Home Depot Inc., the nation's largest home improvement retailer, Tuesday reported a 33 percent rise in profits to a new high for the latest quarter, and the upbeat results sparked a rally in its stock.
The company said it earned $258.8 million or 53 cents a share in its fiscal first quarter ended on May 4, vs. year earlier profits of $195.0 million or 41 cents a share.
Revenues also were up sharply at $5.65 billion from $4.36 billion.
Following the news, Home Depot's stock jumped $1.125 to a 52-week high of $60.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
"Fiscal 1997 is off to a very strong start with our record earnings for the first quarter," said Bernard Marcus, chief executive officer.
"We are particularly pleased with strong sales trends in the first quarter, which reflect an earlier start to the spring season versus last year," he said.

In the first quarter, Home Depot said it opened 24 new stores, bringing the total to 536 stores, including 503 Home Depot stores and 5 EXPO Design Centres in the United States and 28 Home Depot stores in Canada.
